projects.name: bazibo
projects.goal: One app of play-and-learn games for children of 3 to 10: no ads, no trackers, one €1 purchase that opens every game.

phases.name: Bubbels, the first game
phases.summary: the bubble shooter: 30 levels, pop sounds, offline, playable on the web

phases.name: Brand app in the stores
phases.summary: one app with a tile per game, Dutch and English, the €1 unlock behind a parental gate, on Google Play and then the App Store

phases.name: Learning games
phases.summary: games that teach, for children who cannot read yet and for those who can

gap.item: Google Play update to 1.12.0 (version code 14, twenty-two games: Schaken, Ludo with Pachisi, Egeltje, Kangoeroe, Kaartpuzzel, Tijgers en geitjes, Klok Digitaal and the rest since 1.8.0) submitted to internal and production on 19 Nov 2026, replacing 1.10.0 and 1.11.0 before review; in review at Google (the public page still shows 1.8.0, checked 20 Nov)

projects.name: jarvis
projects.goal: Talk to a Claude Code session hands-free from an Android phone, on your own machines, over Tailscale.

phases.name: Weekend test
phases.summary: spoken round trip from the phone (HTTP Shortcuts) to headless Claude Code, local STT/TTS

phases.name: Plugin
phases.summary: machine side as a Claude Code plugin others can install

phases.name: Android app
phases.summary: a native phone client built on the lessons of the test

phases.name: Full agent
phases.summary: Jarvis can do what the coding session can, on its host, under the same rules, with a spoken yes for irreversible actions

phases.name: Voice and speed
phases.summary: Mark (2026-11-16): Jarvis wakes on Mark's voice, hands-free, and answers fast; plus talking without a project

phases.name: Notifications
phases.summary: Jarvis tells the phone that something needs Mark: a build, a question, a reply, a pending confirmation; self-hosted, tailnet-only, no Google

phases.name: Fingerprint confirmation
phases.summary: an irreversible action can be released by a signature from the phone that needs Mark's fingerprint, verified on the agent host

phases.name: Drive mode
phases.summary: the drive as the unit (approved 2026-11-17): where was I, nothing lost, arrivals, a drive log at the desk, then the screen off with the wheel button

gap.item: A spoken round trip from the phone over the tailnet (HTTP Shortcuts)
Android app: a spoken round trip on Mark's phone, recorded in the how-to
Android app: a release build attached to a GitHub release by CI (task 4.3)
Drive mode 2: nothing lost: a turn id runs once, slow turns and dropped connections become arrivals, "what's new", "cancel", an unheard read-back cancelled
Drive mode 3: the app in the drive (arrival and problem tones, one retry under the same turn id) and Mark's parked test
Drive mode 4: the drive log handed to the agent host; the coding session takes up the notes
Drive mode 5: project by voice, the app following the bridge
Drive mode 6: long replies in parts (go on, repeat, back)
Drive mode 7: screen off and the wheel button, then the first use on the road
Full agent: daily line in the notes, and Mark's parked test (merge by voice)
Wake on Mark's voice: hands-free start with a wake word on the phone, and Jarvis reacts only to Mark (speaker verification, #23; proposal in #29, approved by Mark 2026-11-16)

Speed: a typical turn under 10 s (measured 2026-11-16: about 15-25 s; done so far: 4 CPUs, a 160-character spoken answer, streaming speech built and deployed (#66, homelab#74), a fresh session after an hour idle (#68); next: a voice profile and Whisper settings switched on)

Speed: streaming speech live: bridge deployed (homelab#74) and the APK released (android-87bcad4, 2026-11-17); open: Mark's turns on the phone, first_audio_ms of real turns in the how-to and how it sounds at sentence boundaries (task 3.3)

Speed: a voice profile (voice_model, voice_effort) and Whisper settings (language, beam) built and measured, default unchanged; proposed: effort low (about 5 s off multi-step turns, same answers), JARVIS_WHISPER_LANGUAGE=en (0.8 s); not switched on yet

Easter egg (Mark 2026-11-17): Jarvis sings when asked; public-domain tunes on the bridge (happy-birthday, twinkle, frere-jacques, mountain-king, ode-to-joy) plus one marked parody (iron-man, the riff only, own words, JARVIS_SING_PARODY=0 off), the agent's own lyrics, Kokoro plus numpy TD-PSOLA and a soft organ, at most 20 s, never a read-back, JARVIS_SING=0 off; change jarvis-sing built with tests in CI (#78, #79, #81); bridge with every tune deployed 2026-11-17 (homelab#78); open: the prompt installed on the agent host and a song heard on the phone, recorded

Easter egg 2 (Mark 2026-11-18, "Can it beatbox?"): Jarvis beatboxes when asked; three beats on the bridge (boots-and-cats, hip-hop, jarvis-hook with a hummed bass and a sung hook) or one at random, sounds cut from its own Kokoro voice over synthesised drums, numpy only, at most 15 s, never a read-back, JARVIS_BEATBOX=0 off; change jarvis-beatbox built with tests in CI; open: merged, the bridge image deployed, the prompt installed on the agent host and a beat heard on the phone
Claude Code plugin: the gate as a standalone plugin, then the bridge setup

Egress stage 0, observe only (jarvis-credential-proxy): a proxy on loopback under its own user passes every connection of a full turn through by name and logs it (origin, address, TLS server name; never bodies, headers or queries), the turn record gets a summary, egress.mode = off by default, nothing denied; built with tests in CI, reviewed and merged (#87), installed on agent-lxc and live in observe since 2026-11-20 with its host checks passing (traffic through the proxy, timing within noise, desk unchanged, gate checks 4-6 and 12); pinning the proxy variables built (0.13, needs a reinstall); open: a week of voice turns observed, the list for stage 1
Notifications: POST /notify on the bridge, the ntfy broker on the tailnet, the app's listener with fixed words on the lock screen, the battery number measured
Fingerprint confirmation: a signed confirmation verified on the agent host, the method per class, the parked test
Speaker check, phase 0: the measurement of false refusals and false accepts, with a go or no-go
